messages:
sre-oncall: noticing apiserver 503s and controller-manager leader churn in eu2 after a sudden GPU node attach wave at 02:14 UTC.
jules: checking alerts, conntrack_high eu2-gpu = 92% and nat_ports low.
infra-bot: conntrack_count eu2 = 184000 / 200000 ; nat_ephemeral_free = 18 / 16384 :warning:
nina: logs show many kubelet short-lived connects: `E... dial tcp 10.30.1.9:6443: connection reset by peer`.
sre-oncall: likely chain: massive attach -> conntrack + ephemeral port squeeze -> apiserver accept queue pressure -> watcher reconnect storm -> controller-manager backoff -> etcd leader jitter.
omar: mitigation: 1) pause autoscaler for eu2, 2) sysctl bump on nat/gw, 3) move etcd leader if it's on a noisy host. applying hold now.
jules: applying `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=400000` and expanding `ip_local_port_range` on gateways; rolling.
infra-bot: sysctl rollout completed -> 6/6 gateways updated :white_check_mark:
omar: leader relocated to eu2-a-01 after marking noisy host unsched; etcd commit latency back to baseline.
sre-oncall: apiserver 5xxs falling, controller-manager stable. follow-ups: add autoscaler startup smear, add ephemeral port headroom alert, and document runbook.
jules: will draft RFC for GPU scale safety limits and add probe for rapid attach patterns.
sre-oncall: incident logged, monitoring for 30m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread summarizing eu2 control plane instabilities tied to GPU provisioning surge causing conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion and short etcd/apiserver impact.
